result.summary: Our patch closes the CWE-094 flaw the same way the official fix does — it enforces a base-type (isAssignableFrom) allowlist before any reflective construction — but centralizes it in a reusable MappingUtil.loadClass helper and routes property creation through the already-guarded PropertyFactory. Every production sink the official fix touches (PropertiesParser, YamlParser, XmlParser property + flipstrategy paths, PropertyFactory.createProperty, MappingUtil.instanceFlippingStrategy, and both ConsoleOperations methods) is covered. POV no longer reproduces and 5 regressions pass. This is functionally equivalent to the reference fix with a cleaner, centralized implementation.
result.root_cause: Config/web-console parsers pass attacker-controlled fully-qualified class names into Class.forName(...).newInstance()/getConstructor(...).newInstance() with no type restriction, allowing arbitrary class loading and constructor execution (code injection).

dimensions.rationale: Every reflective sink now verifies expectedType.isAssignableFrom before construction, so arbitrary attacker class names are rejected — the class, not just the observed payload, is closed.
dimensions.evidence: MappingUtil.loadClass() isAssignableFrom check; PropertyFactory.createProperty now calls loadClass(pType, Property.class); all three parsers + ConsoleOperations route through loadClass
dimensions.label: Vulnerability elimination

dimensions.rationale: Fixes at the trust boundary by centralizing the type-restriction guard before instantiation rather than patching a single caller.
dimensions.evidence: new MappingUtil.loadClass(className, expectedType) used by PropertiesParser/YamlParser/XmlParser/ConsoleOperations; PropertyFactory guarded too
dimensions.label: Root cause vs symptom

issues.description: Type restriction is base-type (Property/FlippingStrategy) rather than an explicit class allowlist — same limitation as the official fix; a malicious class implementing those interfaces could still be constructed, but this matches developer intent.
loadClass uses raw Class<? extends Property> generics in PropertyFactory, producing unchecked-warning-level rawness; no functional impact.
